FLUXINI · PRODUCT REVIEW · 27 SEPTEMBER 2026

Make the first good result easy.

A UI/UX review and next-release plan for Fluxini. Start with the creative task, reveal technical depth when it is useful, and make the exported result match the preview.

Current build: 0.3Windows firstSmall teamProposed work, not implemented
0.4 update: The first usability package is implemented. This review preserves the original 0.3 evidence; later milestones remain planned.

Next release: usability before breadth

The current engine already demonstrates text, particles, water and clouds. The interface still asks the user to think in operators, node connections and solver parameters too early. Build a clear path from an idea to a finished short clip.

Recommended first action: spend the next two weeks improving the existing workflow: relevant actions, readable controls, keyboard behavior, panel hierarchy and trustworthy starters.

    Interaction principles

    Keep the manual workflow complete

    AI should be a shortcut for an understandable edit. A user must still be able to create, change, recover and export without a model connection. The existing Flux/Claude integration stays in place.

    Architecture that supports the UX

    Outcome-based milestones

    Assumption: two engineers plus a product designer who can run user sessions. Approximately 63–95 engineering days, with a 10–14 calendar-week planning envelope for integration, testing and platform uncertainty. Re-estimate for actual staffing. These are not delivery promises.

    M1Understandable workflowM2Motion compositionM3Simulation + deliveryM4Useful Flux assistanceM5Windows beta

    Critical path: M1 → M2 → M3 → M5. M4 can overlap after selection and recipe contracts settle. Start bounded packaging and export feasibility spikes during M1.

    The next two weeks, concretely

    WhenWorkReviewable result

    Deliberately deferred

      Define success before adding more features

      All targets below are proposed acceptance criteria. None is presented as an improvement already measured in a participant study.

      MeasureTargetHow to check it

      Observe real tasks

      First, recruit five people from the intended audience. Ask them to start a scene, change its appearance, coordinate text and an effect, undo a mistake, find their saved project and export a short clip. Observe wrong turns, time, help requests and whether the result matches their intention. Avoid teaching the graph model first.

      Repeat with 5–8 people in the private beta. These are formative samples, not population-level conversion claims. Record only with consent. Test integrated and discrete GPU machines, Windows scaling and the actual desktop shell before declaring system requirements.

      Open decisions

      1. Confirm the primary audience; the current assumption is motion designers with limited 3D experience.
      2. Confirm that short clips are the primary output rather than still images or editable DCC assets.
      3. Choose supported Windows hardware and scaling from measured tests.
      4. Validate font import and local video encoding paths before committing formats.
      5. Decide how much physically plausible behavior versus stylized control the first beta needs.

      The first keyboard, action-relevance, readability and layout fixes can proceed while these decisions are validated.

      Evidence and reference guidance

      This review is a planning artifact. Application code and saved scenes were not changed. Full implementation detail is saved alongside it in Fluxini-UX-Review-and-Roadmap.md. Review source data and screenshots are in artifacts/ux-review.
